source_records.statement: Four original editable vectors were authored for Figure Studio from scientific method concepts supported by primary research articles. Paths, layouts, and illustrative marks were constructed anew; no proprietary asset, published diagram, screenshot, tracing, image, or third-party vector component was incorporated.

scientific_references.citation: Macosko et al. Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets. Cell 161, 1202–1214 (2015).
scientific_references.use: Method concepts only: aqueous cell partitioning, oligo-barcoded capture beads, shared bead barcodes, distinct molecular identifiers, and poly(dT) capture. No published artwork, geometry, image, or sequence was copied.

scientific_references.citation: Ståhl et al. Visualization and analysis of gene expression in tissue sections by spatial transcriptomics. Science 353, 78–82 (2016).
scientific_references.use: Method concept only: a tissue section associated with spatially barcoded capture positions. No single-cell resolution claim, published image, or measured expression pattern is reproduced.

scientific_references.citation: Raj et al. Imaging individual mRNA molecules using multiple singly labeled probes. Nature Methods 5, 877–879 (2008).
scientific_references.use: Method concept only: RNA-probe-associated puncta in a cellular field with nuclear context. No microscopy image, measured spot positions, molecular counts, target genes, or scale was copied.

artwork_refinement.statement: Four existing original method schematics were refined as new editable vector geometry, informed by the recorded primary-source method concepts. No source artwork, tracing, raster data, experimental sequences or measurements were incorporated.

scientific_references.design_decision: Cell/bead compartment, oligo(dT) capture, shared cell barcode and distinct molecular identifiers. No guarantee of one cell/bead per droplet. Drop-seq RT location must not generalize to all methods.
Tissue on spatially barcoded capture features with distinct probe roles; feature is not necessarily a single cell. No measured expression map, intensity or platform spacing.
Probe hybridization versus tethered amplification; HCR hairpins/initiators are DNA. Use relationship precedent only, do not impose HCR chemistry on generic RNA FISH.

scientific_references.figure: Methods/abstract only; figure pixels not examined
scientific_references.design_decision: Multiple singly labelled probes support schematic RNA-associated cellular puncta. No measured positions, counts, target identity, scale or copied microscopy.

scientific_references.figure: Methods only; figure pixels not used
scientific_references.design_decision: Nuclei isolation and nucleus/bead co-encapsulation clarify sample context only; no measured figure layout or exact branded sample-preparation protocol.

assets.name: Microfluidic Cell Partition
assets.description: Original plan-view schematic of aqueous cell suspension pinching into separated droplets at an oil-flow junction. An occupied and an empty droplet illustrate non-guaranteed single-cell occupancy. Device geometry, occupancy and sizes are not experimental measurements.

scientific_references.citation: Macosko et al. Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets. Cell 161, 1202–1214 (2015).
scientific_references.use: Method concepts only: aqueous cell partitioning, oligo-barcoded capture beads, shared bead barcodes, distinct molecular identifiers, and poly(dT) capture. No published artwork, geometry, image, or sequence was copied.

scientific_limitations: Schematic device, flow direction, droplet size, and cell number; not a scaled device design.
Droplet partitioning does not guarantee one cell per droplet; empty droplets and multiplets can occur.
This asset depicts partitioning only; use the separate capture-bead asset for barcoded RNA capture.

assets.name: Oligo-barcoded RNA Capture Bead
assets.description: Original capture-bead schematic with six illustrative oligonucleotide tethers. Shared barcode segments match; molecular-identifier segment shapes vary; terminal segments indicate poly(dT) capture. Shapes are not nucleotide sequences and tether count does not encode oligonucleotide density.

scientific_references.citation: Macosko et al. Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets. Cell 161, 1202–1214 (2015).
scientific_references.use: Method concepts only: aqueous cell partitioning, oligo-barcoded capture beads, shared bead barcodes, distinct molecular identifiers, and poly(dT) capture. No published artwork, geometry, image, or sequence was copied.

scientific_limitations: Shared barcode means common bead identity; it does not establish successful single-cell occupancy.
Molecular identifier sequences differ among capture oligonucleotides; the drawn segment shapes are not sequence encodings.
A simplified tether arrangement omits protocol-specific handles and does not show a measured oligonucleotide density.

assets.name: Tissue-associated Spatial RNA Capture Array
assets.description: Original plan-view tissue context over regularly spaced spatially barcoded capture positions. Capture positions are not cells or measured expression; a position may collect RNA from multiple cells. Tissue shape, array pitch and count are illustrative.

scientific_references.citation: Ståhl et al. Visualization and analysis of gene expression in tissue sections by spatial transcriptomics. Science 353, 78–82 (2016).
scientific_references.use: Method concept only: a tissue section associated with spatially barcoded capture positions. No single-cell resolution claim, published image, or measured expression pattern is reproduced.

scientific_limitations: Capture positions are not cells; an individual position may capture RNA from multiple cells.
The array pitch, capture-site size, tissue outline, and number of sites are illustrative and imply no single-cell resolution.
No gene, expression magnitude, anatomical diagnosis, or measured tissue dataset is represented.
